{"id":"persona-5s4b.22","title":"unsafe blocks without SAFETY comments (4 sites)","description":"Four `unsafe` blocks carry no `// SAFETY:` comment. rust.md: "SAFETY comment on every unsafe block. No exceptions."

- personad/src/main.rs:53 — `let uid = unsafe { libc::getuid() };`
- persona-nmh/src/main.rs:62 — `let uid = unsafe { libc::getuid() };`
- persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:20 — `let my_uid = unsafe { libc::getuid() };`
- persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:56-64 — `unsafe { libc::getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERCRED, &mut ucred as *mut _ as *mut _, &mut len) }`

The convention already exists in this repo: persona/src/main.rs:56 and :392 both carry `// SAFETY: getuid() has no preconditions and always succeeds.` The four above were simply missed.

The getsockopt block is the one with real invariants to state and the only one where a future edit can introduce UB: the raw pointer must point to a live `libc::ucred`, `len` must match its size on entry, and `fd` must be an open AF_UNIX socket fd owned by `stream` for the duration of the call. With no SAFETY comment, a later change (e.g. swapping the struct, or taking a RawFd from a dropped stream) has nothing to check itself against.

Fix: add SAFETY comments stating the invariants.
